Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-08-20 | AAPL | Underweight | +1.1% | -0.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL: trim 25–35% of current exposure to a 65–75% core of standard AAPL weight, blended rather than in one print — roughly half near 311.30–313.00 and the balance as limits into 315.52–320.28 if a bounce is offered; complete the trim on a daily close below 310.69. Do not add anywhere between 300 and 320. Reserve only 20–25% of a standard allocation as half-sized, confirmation-based tactical capital: a first tranche only in 302–306 after stabilization above 300.00 (a 299.00 stop can be skipped, two >6% gaps in five weeks), the second only on a daily close above 320.28 on ≥65M shares. A close below 300.00 on expanding volume cuts the residual toward the 289.77 and 281.30 references; a reclaim of 320.28 on real volume, or a Q4 FY26 gross margin ≥50% after the EU take-rate reset, restores the rating. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is settled by convergence, degree is where the money is made, and on degree the three seats overreach in the same direction — they want to sell more than the evidence at 311.30 supports.

What the bear wins, and it is the only dated, undisputed evidence in the debate: AAPL gapped −7.35% on 132.5M shares (~2.5x average) on 2026-07-31 after the 10-Q was accepted, the largest volume print available, and that gap is still unfilled — price sits 6.64% below the pre-report close and 9.66% below the 344.57 high. On 08-19/08-20 AAPL tagged 320.28 and was rejected, closing 311.30, just 0.65 above the session low and 0.61 above the gap's lower edge at 310.69. The advance into it printed 101% and 95% of the twenty-day average volume; a genuine gap-fill breakout prints 130–150%. RSI made lower highs at 72 → 54 → 49 with no bullish divergence, and price is below the 315.52 Bollinger middle/20-day mean, inside the 315.52–320.28 resistance stack. Reward/risk from 311.30 is roughly 0.8:1 to the 320.28 rejection high against the 300.00 base floor. Layered on top: ~35x FY2026 EPS on roughly $8.90, a rising effective tax rate at 17.58% (+219bp), R&D +32.5%, buybacks decelerated 12% to $62.1B, inventory +94% with raw materials +260%, ~$13.3B of intangibles with no matching acquisition outflow and ~$13.5B of unexplained other noncurrent liabilities, and an EU App Store take-rate reset (26% Apple IAP, 20% alternative payments, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission) effective October 1 with no quantified revenue impact in the file. An unknown is not neutral when the good news has been bought.

What the bull wins, and why this is not Sell or a 40–50% cut: nothing reported has broken. Nine-month revenue +16.15%, gross margin 49.07% with Q3 at 50.06%, EPS +22.42%, FCF $110.2B, net cash up $28.5B to ~$62.2B with no new long-term issuance, a −63 day cash conversion cycle, and price 10.67% above a rising 200-day at 281.30 with the golden cross intact and the 50-day at 309.85 flat rather than rolling over. And the tape is improving, not deteriorating: the MACD histogram has contracted for six straight sessions from −3.34 to −0.46, the 10-EMA/50-SMA/VWMA are compressed into a 2.16-point band, and VWMA turned up on 08-20 for the first time in ten sessions. The conservative seat's decisive contribution — that with ATR at 7.81 and two >6% single-day gaps in five weeks (06-25, 07-31) a stop is a wish, so size is the binding control — cuts against its own conclusion: it argues for less exposure and smaller tactical size, not for leaning to the top of the cut band while the primary trend is intact.

Where each seat loses. The aggressive analyst is right on the tape and wrong to dress a trim as a high-conviction reload: a 299.00 stop does not define six points of risk in an instrument that jumped 20+ points overnight twice in five weeks, and his limit-only execution into 315.52–320.28 assumes a bounce the market just refused to deliver. The conservative analyst is right on the information vacuum and wrong to near-freeze re-entry until the FY26 filing, which strands the caller holding a full core with no plan and repeats the GOOGL error of ossifying an Underweight into a permanent one. The neutral analyst is the best-balanced and supplies the correct execution note — blended tranches, complete the trim below 310.69 rather than waiting for a bounce — but a 35–45% cut is too large when the falsification level (320.28) is only 2.9% above spot.

That proximity is the deciding arithmetic, and my own record makes it binding. The 06-30, 07-01, 07-13 and 07-20 through 07-24 AAPL Underweights each gave up 3–9% of five-day alpha by trimming momentum decay inside an intact uptrend; the 08-13 reflection codified the fix as requiring the high-volume distribution print, and the 08-12 reflection as sizing the rating by distance-to-invalidation, noting an Underweight whose falsification sits ~3% above entry has poor expectancy. Here the distribution print is real (07-31) but it is twenty sessions old and price has climbed 3.6% off the 300.57 low, price is back marginally above VWMA, and the upgrade gate is 2.9% away against a 3.6% drop to the 300 floor. That is a modestly negative skew, not a decisive one — so trim, but smaller than the Research Manager's 30–50% and smaller than the neutral's 35–45%: cut 25–35%, leaning to the larger end only if 315.52–320.28 is offered.

What would change the rating. Upgrade toward Hold/Overweight on a daily close above 320.28 on ≥65M shares with MACD above zero, or on a Q4 FY2026 print with gross margin holding ≥50% after the EU changes — either restores the trimmed exposure in tranches. Downgrade to Sell on a daily close below 300.00 on expanding volume (cutting to the 289.77 then 281.30 references), on Q4 gross margin below 48%, or if the FY26 10-K shows the $13.3B intangible build is a capitalized commitment carrying amortization or impairment risk, or that inventory days fail to normalize below ~12.

Data gaps, stated rather than papered over: no sentiment report was supplied in this run, no options chain or implied-volatility data (so the hedge the neutral seat favors cannot be priced here), only 20 of 118 eligible news records with zero coverage of 2026-08-13 through 08-17 and no record explaining the 07-31 gap, no consensus forward EPS or valuation multiple, no resolved intangibles footnote, and no portfolio context — so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation, and the target is technical, not valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 305.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
Alpha of −0.1% versus SPY on a +1.1% raw return says the Underweight call cost essentially nothing in five days, but a five-day window cannot adjudicate a 1–3 month thesis built on a 320.28 invalidation 2.9% away — it is too short to judge, and −0.1% is noise. What the window does support is the sizing logic: neither the 320.28 reclaim nor the 310.69/300.00 breakdown fired, so the "modest negative skew, not a decisive one" framing that produced a 25–35% trim rather than 40–50% was the right posture, while the bear's gap-fill and rejection case remains entirely unconfirmed. Lesson for next time: when the falsification level sits under 3% above spot and the trigger prints are that close, state the entry as conditional on the trigger rather than pre-positioning ahead of it, so the five-day mark reflects a decision instead of a drift.

[2026-08-19 | AAPL | Overweight | -1.1% | -0.7% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AAPL, built in tranches rather than bought at spot. Take only a starter of roughly one-sixth of a standard full allocation (half of the trader's tranche one) at ~316.83, and only while AAPL is holding above the 307.8–309.4 pivot cluster (VWMA 307.76 / 50-SMA 309.44); treat 305.50 as a disaster stop, not a guaranteed exit, because the 2026-07-31 session gapped −7.35% and that gap is twice the 3.6% stop distance. Add tranche two (~one-third of allocation) only on a MACD bullish crossover confirmed by a daily close above 319.28 on ≥55M shares (ideally 65M+), raising the stop to ~309.44 once filled; add tranche three only on a daily close above 329.59, where the position may go to 1.25× standard. Closes below 309.44 then 307.76 suspend all adds (do not average down), a close under 300.00 halves the position, and the rising 200-SMA at 281.10 — not 305.50 — is the final thesis line. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is not the contested question; entry geometry is, and that is what fixes the rating at Overweight rather than Buy.

The structural side of the debate went to the bull unopposed. The bear did not dispute the operating record — FQ3 revenue +16.36% to $109.4B, gross margin 50.06%, operating margin 32.62%, diluted EPS +28.66%, nine-month revenue +16.15%, nine-month FCF $110.2B at ~30% of revenue, operating cash flow 1.15× net income, net cash +$28.4B to $62.2B, $14.4B of debt retired with zero new long-term debt, buybacks of $62.1B plus $11.8B of dividends funded internally — he argued only that it is visible. The primary trend corroborates: the close of 316.83 is 12.71% above a 200-SMA of 281.10 that has risen ~40 straight sessions, with the 50-SMA at 309.44 still 28.3 points above it. My own record reinforces the point: the 07-13, 07-20, 07-21 and 07-22 AAPL Underweights each forfeited 3.2%–6.2% of five-day alpha by trimming momentum decay inside a stacked rising structure, and the 2026-08-12 Underweight (+4.8% raw, +5.3% alpha) was simply the wrong side of a repair that was already underway. Fighting a rising 200-SMA on a fortress balance sheet is the losing side of that coin flip.

The tactical side went to the bears, and their arithmetic corrections are adopted rather than argued with. The aggressive desk's 1.6:1 payoff claim does not survive: if his own trigger is a close above 319.28, entry cannot also be 316.83, and from 316.83 the reward to the 329.59 gap top is ~10.3 points against ~11.33 points of risk to 305.50 — roughly 0.91:1, not 1.6:1. A 0.79-point close above the 316.04 Bollinger mid is 0.1 ATR of noise, not a regime shift; MACD at −1.719 versus a −0.984 signal is a repair (histogram improved from −3.634 on 08-05 to −0.735 on 08-19) that still needs a zero-line reclaim; and 50.51M shares at 0.95× the 53.04M 20-day average (1.03× ex-outlier) with a VWMA that has slid 21 sessions from 329.58 to 307.76 is not accumulation. AAPL is closed inside the unfilled 310.69–329.59 gap created by a −7.35% day on 132.49M shares — real trapped supply overhead — and the July breakdown is not neutralized until 329.59 is reclaimed.

The conservative desk's gap argument is the one that changes sizing, and the neutral desk supplied the number. A close-basis stop cannot control a name that just gapped 7.35%; that gap is roughly double the 3.6% stop distance, so tranche one is exposed to a loss larger than planned. With full allocation ≈28% notional for 1% of portfolio risk at an 11.33-point stop, a full one-third tranche (~9.3% notional) would lose ~0.68% of portfolio on a July-31-style gap before any later adds — too much of the 0.75–1.0% budget spent on the most unconfirmed leg. Halving the starter to ~one-sixth (~4.7% notional) costs ~0.35% of portfolio in the same scenario and preserves room for the higher-probability adds. The conservative prescription of zero exposure until 319.28 is rejected on the neutral's own geometry: buying at 319.28 against the same 305.50 stop widens risk to 13.78 points (4.3%) and worsens the ratio unless the stop is raised to ~309.44, so waiting is not free — it just moves the risk from gap to chase.

Why not Underweight, and why not Hold. The bear's central pricing claim — "premium valuation" — is as unevidenced as the bull's Services-margin inference he criticizes: the fact set contains no multiples, no consensus, no guidance. He cannot debit an evidence gap he shares. His own recommendation is explicitly not a short against a $62B net-cash balance sheet; he is arguing about entry price, not direction. And a Hold misprices the asymmetry the primary trend creates: the payoff is bounded below by a 3.6% stop and a defined pivot cluster, while a close above 329.59 opens the July shelf at 333–340 and the 344.57 high.

Unresolved risks that justify tranching rather than committing: inventory +94% to $11.1B with raw materials +260% set against finished goods −4% (a component pre-buy or a demand bet — the FY26 10-K is the arbiter); intangibles net +91% to $25.417B against only ~$1.2B of nine-month amortization, implying a forward operating-income drag; other noncurrent liabilities +$13.5B/+32.6% to $55.08B with no footnote; the EU take-rate reset effective October 1 (26% IAP / 20% alt payments / 15% link-outs / 5% Core Technology Commission) as both an estimate-revision vector and a precedent template; effective tax rate normalizing from 15.39% to 17.58% (~200bp, ~$2.5B/yr); R&D +32.5% to 9.34% of revenue capping operating leverage; and buybacks down 12% YoY to $62.1B, confirming capital allocation is policy, not a price floor.

What would change the rating. Upgrade to Buy on a daily close above 329.59 on sustained volume expansion, or on an FQ4 print with gross margin ≥49.5%, inventory flat-to-down, and the evidence gaps filled. Move to Underweight on a decisive close below 305.50, on a close under 300.00 un-reclaimed, or on FQ4 gross margin materially below 48.5% with revenue growth decelerating and inventory building. Stated gaps, not papered over: no segment or geographic revenue, no valuation multiples, no consensus estimates or revision trend, no guidance, no insider data, no options/implied-vol data, and a news feed covering only 20 of 143 records with a five-day hole from August 12–16 — the cause of the July 31 gap remains unestablished, so the 310.69–329.59 gap is carried as unquantified event risk, and every target here is technical, not valuation-derived. No portfolio context was provided, so all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation and must respect their single-name and mega-cap concentration caps.

**Price Target**: 329.59

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY26 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of −0.7% (raw −1.1%) is directionally wrong but too small and too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis built on tranches above 319.28 and 329.59; the entry trigger was never hit, so the window mostly tests the starter only. It undercuts the claim that the pivot cluster at 307.8–309.4 was holding — the drift lower from 316.83 is exactly the "no accumulation" read the bear desk supplied, and supports the halved sizing rather than the Overweight framing. Lesson: when the entry trigger sits 0.8% above spot, rate the structure, not the position — say explicitly that a 5-day move below the trigger is expected noise and define what price action in that window would actually falsify the call.

[2026-08-18 | AAPL | Hold | -0.0% | +0.2% | 5d]

**Executive Summary**: Hold AAPL: maintain the core position at the standard 4–5% of portfolio NAV, initiate nothing at 310.03, and do nothing at all between 302.25 and 311.49 — that band is noise inside an unresolved range, not an entry. Trim the tactical sleeve into 316.49, then 321.66–323.45, then 329.59, holding the core through the late-October FQ4 print and FY26 10-K.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate resolves to Hold, and unlike a lazy fence-sit this one is arithmetic: the bull case owns the business, the bear case owns the entry, and neither converts the other.

Why the bull does not get an add. AAPL closed at 310.03, below the unfilled 07-31 gap floor at 310.69 and below the bull's own 311.49 trigger. The "average-stack reclaim" of the 10-EMA (308.99), 50-SMA (309.13) and VWMA (309.70) is 0.04–0.14 ATR of clearance on each measure — statistically indistinguishable from touching the cluster. The 08-18 tape printed 53.4M shares, below the trader's own 55M volume condition and only ~40% of the 132.5M capitulation print of 07-31, and the VWMA has fallen twenty consecutive sessions from 329.58 to 309.70, i.e. real trapped supply sits just overhead. Momentum repair is real but incomplete: the MACD histogram contracted five sessions from −3.634 to −1.659 and the 10-EMA printed its first uptick since 07-30, yet MACD remains below zero at −2.459 against a still-falling signal at −0.800, and RSI at 47.86 offers no cushion. The aggressive analyst's central move — sizing off the 329.59 gap at ~1.39:1 — ignores that between 311.50 and the gap sit four shelves starting at 316.49, only ~5 points above entry against a 13-point stop, and the honest first-target ratio is ~0.38:1. He also waives the plan's own volume condition and leans on the Rothschild Redburn upgrade as institutional confirmation when the supplied news set is explicitly self-contradictory (a Buy and two cautious/bearish pieces inside the same 60-minute window on 08-17, with the target magnitude unverifiable). Sizing 1.0–1.5% NAV on that is paying up for a coin flip, and the stored lesson from 2026-08-05 — an AAPL Overweight that deployed a starter at ~311 ahead of its own 311.80/>65M gate and surrendered −3.1% of five-day alpha — is the direct precedent.
